newsitem.title: CANADA: Amax, Bema start Refugio production.
newsitem.headline: Amax, Bema start Refugio production.

text.p: Amax Gold Inc and Bema Gold Corp said on Friday that their jointly owned Refugio gold mine in Chile reached commercial production on October 1.
All the mine's crushers were operating and surpassed design capacity rates of 30,000 tonnes of half-inch ore per day, the companies said.
The mechanical and structural problems at the fine crushing plant were resolved, they said.
More than 5.5 million tonnes had been placed on leach pads and about 64,000 ounces had been recovered since the first gold was poured in mid-April.
The mine is expected to produce an average of 233,000 ounces of gold a year at cash costs averaging at US$235 an ounce.
The companies also said they planned to start a drilling program on the Pancho deposit on the Refugio property.
The Refugio mine is operated by Cia Minera Maricunga, owned 50 percent by Amax and 50 percent by Bema.
